# SCL for a developer

> **Reader:** developer. **Already knows:** the stack, the patterns, and how code is built. **Next step:** understand, then build within these constraints. **Human-constraint budget:** ~14 min read · cognitive load **M**.

The model is the source of truth. This narrative is generated from it.

## Judgements a person owns

Validation cannot certify these. A human owns the judgement.

- `outcome-backwards-compatibility` ⚖ A person decides whether older projects still work, where that is practical.
- `outcome-context-survives` ⚖ A new person can reconstruct the reasons from the project alone.
- `outcome-ai-outcome-aligned` ⚖ A person can tell whether the generated work still serves the outcome.
- `outcome-ai-understanding-inspectable` ⚖ You can read what the assistant assumed before any build starts.
- `outcome-reviewers-understand-min-constraint` ⚖ The write-up is as short as it can be without hiding a risk the reader owns.
- `outcome-uncertainty-visible` ⚖ Open risks stay on a single list, and a recommendation that depends on one says so.
- `outcome-prerequisites-verified` ⚖ Work stops when a critical skill is missing, and says what to restore.
- `outcome-constraints-reliable-not-restrictive` ⚖ Rules block real violations and still allow a new approach that follows the rules.
- `outcome-verification-role-aligned` ⚖ The project checks the right scope and does not keep a second, drifting copy of the truth.

## Releases are consistent and reproducible

Outcomes: `outcome-consistent-frameworks`, `outcome-reproducible-releases`.

The interaction that turns tagged source into a consumable release.

- `requirement-versioned` (delivery, implemented). Every release carries a version that matches its folder name. Acceptance: Given a release folder named v0.1.0, when its manifest is read, then version is 0.1.0.
- `requirement-change-docs` (governance, implemented). Every release explains what changed. Acceptance: Given a release folder, when it is checked, then RELEASE.md and CHANGELOG.md exist.
- `requirement-reproducible` (delivery, implemented). Each release kit matches the source snapshot recorded for that release. Acceptance: Given a release, when its kit is compared with that release's source snapshot, then every file matches and the digest matches.
- `requirement-self-contained` (architectural, implemented). A release folder copied on its own does not point outside itself. Acceptance: Given the release folder, when its text files are scanned, then none contain a network URL, an absolute home path, or a link that leaves the folder.

## Release quality gates

Outcomes: `outcome-consistent-frameworks`.

The interaction that applies the release quality gates.

- `requirement-validation-instructions` (governance, implemented). Each release tells a consumer how to validate it. Acceptance: Given a release folder, when it is checked, then VALIDATION_CHECKLIST.md exists.

## Upgrades are predictable

Outcomes: `outcome-predictable-upgrades`, `outcome-backwards-compatibility` ⚖.

The interaction in which a maintainer publishes how to move off the previous release.

- `requirement-upgrade-instructions` (delivery, implemented). Every release after the first explains how to move off the previous one. Acceptance: Given a second release folder v0.2.0 after v0.1.0, when it is checked, then UPGRADE_FROM_v0.1.0.md exists. The first release does not need one.

## A release only when consumers are affected

Outcomes: `outcome-predictable-upgrades`, `outcome-releases-mean-consumer-impact`.

The interaction that decides whether a change set is allowed to become a release.

- `requirement-release-eligibility` (governance, implemented). A release is cut only when a project-consumable asset changed. Internal-only edits are recorded as framework work, not a release. Acceptance: Given a change set of only meta/ and changelog/ paths, when eligibility is classified, then the result is no release. Given a change under src/schemas/, the result is release.
- `requirement-consumer-impact-test` (governance, implemented). Before a release, answer whether a project on the previous release would behave differently. NO prohibits the release. There is no first-release exception. Acceptance: Given a release, when RELEASE.md is read, then Consumer impact is YES and a behavioural difference of at least 20 characters is recorded. NO is a failed release. The release change list must include a consumer asset.

Outcomes: `outcome-releases-mean-consumer-impact`, `outcome-predictable-upgrades`.

The interaction that moves a meta-model from candidate to a human green light.

- `requirement-lifecycle-four-steps` (governance, implemented). A release candidate is generated from the model, tested, and shipped only on a documented human green light. Acceptance: Given RELEASE.md, when it is read, then the four lifecycle markers are present, including a Green light line.
- `requirement-model-is-source-of-truth` (governance, implemented). Generated documents are derived from the model. When they disagree, the model wins and the document is regenerated. - `requirement-ai-test-before-release` (delivery, implemented). Strict validation, framework self-validation, and the engine tests pass before a candidate is offered for green light. Acceptance: Given RELEASE.md, when it is read, then it records imk validate --strict and validate-framework.py.

## The model captures why

Outcomes: `outcome-intent-visible`, `outcome-context-survives` ⚖, `outcome-ai-outcome-aligned` ⚖.

The interaction in which an author records why the work exists, in the repository, and refuses to invent a missing interaction.

- `requirement-capture-why` (governance, implemented). The model records why the work exists, not only the rules, and every rule traces back to that why. Acceptance: Given the model, when validate runs, then there is at least 1 Intent and 1 Outcome, and every Requirement reaches an Intent.
- `requirement-context-persistent-inspectable` (non-functional, implemented). A new person or a new session can reconstruct the contextual network from the repository alone. Acceptance: Given every evidence pointer, when it is opened, then the file is inside the repository and the anchor is present.
- `requirement-raise-gap-challenge` (governance, implemented). A suspected missing interaction becomes a challenge with an observation, a concern, possibilities, and a question. It is not added as a fact. Acceptance: Given a gap challenge, when it is formatted, then it contains POTENTIAL MODEL GAP and the four labels, and it writes no model file.
- `requirement-model-holds-test-preconditions` (governance, planned). Preconditions, the trigger, and the expected result live in the model before any test is written. Acceptance: Given a future test record, when it is derived, then its precondition, trigger, and expected result already exist on the model. Not enforced in 0.1.0.

- `requirement-emergent-design-surfaced` (governance, planned). A design choice no requirement dictated, which would shape what a person sees, becomes a proposed decision. Incidental choices stay free. Acceptance: Given a material undesigned choice, when it is surfaced, then a Decision with status proposed exists. Not enforced in 0.1.0.

## Unresolved uncertainty stays visible

Outcomes: `outcome-uncertainty-visible` ⚖.

The interaction that keeps one list of unresolved questions and makes recommendations name the ones they depend on.

- `requirement-open-questions-central` (governance, implemented). meta/open-questions.md is the only independent list. Anything else refers to a question by id. Acceptance: Given the repository, when files named open-questions*.md are listed, then the only one is meta/open-questions.md.
- `requirement-open-question-fields` (governance, implemented). Each question has eleven fields, and the risk level is one of Critical, High, Medium, Low, or Informational. Acceptance: Given meta/open-questions.md, when it is parsed, then each question has the eleven named fields and a risk level from that set.
- `requirement-open-question-influence` (governance, implemented). A recommendation that depends on an unresolved High or Critical question names it, names the risk, and says results may change once it is resolved. Acceptance: Given docs/recommendations.md and OQ-001 at High, when the recommendation depends on it, then the text names OQ-001, High, and says results may change.

## Required skills are verified first

Outcomes: `outcome-prerequisites-verified` ⚖.

The interaction that discovers skills, verifies them, and only then runs a significant operation.

- `requirement-skills-registry` (governance, implemented). meta/required-skills.md lists each skill with five fields: id, name, purpose, criticality, and verification. Acceptance: Given meta/required-skills.md, when it is parsed, then every skill has those five fields and a known criticality.
- `requirement-verify-skills-before-ops` (governance, implemented). The harness discovers skills, verifies them, and only then runs the operation. A missing critical skill stops the run and names the skill, the impact, and the action. Acceptance: Given a registry whose critical skill file is missing, when validate runs, then it exits with a FAIL report and does not continue.

- `requirement-no-expressiveness-penalty` (governance, implemented). Only a real boundary violation may fail a solution. Failing a new approach that still follows the rules is a defect.
